sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: Two contracting methods are used for permanent soil nail walls: Procedural (Method) Approach — all design details, materials, and construction methods are specified by the Owner's engineer; and Performance-Based (Design/Build) Approach — the Owner defines geometric, aesthetic, and performance requirements while the Contractor performs the structural design. Method selection depends on project criticality and complexity, Owner experience, and contractor availability. Both approaches are valid if properly implemented.
sections.body: Two types of contracting methods can be used to develop contract drawings and specifications for permanent soil nail wall systems. Some Owners prefer one approach over the other, or a combination of the two approaches. The contracting method is selected based on: the criticality and complexity of the project, the experience of the Owner and their engineering consultants, and the availability of specialty contractors. Both contracting approaches are valid if properly implemented, and each has advantages and potential disadvantages. Procedural or Method Approach: all details of design, construction materials, and methods are specified by the Owner's design engineer. Performance-Based or Design/Build Approach: the Owner defines performance criteria and the Contractor is responsible for completing the structural design.
key_points: Two contracting approaches: Procedural (Method) and Performance-Based (Design/Build)
Procedural: Owner's engineer provides complete design; Contractor prices defined product
Performance-based: Owner sets criteria and geometry; Contractor designs and builds
Method selection based on project complexity, Owner experience, contractor availability
Both approaches require the same three geotechnical analyses (Section 8.2)
sections.applicability: Selection of contracting approach for permanent soil nail wall projects.

sections.title: Geotechnical Analyses Required by Specifications
sections.summary: Three geotechnical analyses are required under either contracting approach: global stability, deformation, and soil corrosivity/corrosion protection class determination. These analyses may be performed by the Owner's engineer in the geotechnical report and included in contract documents, or required as Contractor submittals — in which case adequate time must be allowed in the bid schedule. Before bid document preparation, the Owner must conduct corrosivity testing per Chapter 4 to determine the corrosion protection class and design life.
sections.body: Whether the procedural or performance approach is followed, there are three essential analyses that must be conducted as part of the feasibility assessment of a soil nail wall: global stability analysis, deformation analysis, and soil corrosivity/corrosion protection class determination. These analyses may be performed as part of the geotechnical report included in the contract documents, performed by the Owner, or required as submittals from the Contractor. If required of the Contractor, ample time must be supplied by bid documents to permit the Contractor to conduct their own subsurface investigation and analyses. Before the preparation of bid documents, the Owner must perform corrosivity testing on representative soil samples per Chapter 4 to determine the class of corrosion protection required. The corrosion class and design life are generally specified by the Owner and used by the Contractor regardless of the contracting approach.
key_points: Three mandatory analyses: global stability, deformation, soil corrosivity/corrosion protection class
Analyses may be Owner-performed (included in contract documents) or required Contractor submittals
If Contractor performs analyses, bid schedule must allow adequate time for subsurface investigation
Owner must perform corrosivity testing (Chapter 4) before bid documents are prepared
Corrosion protection class and design life are Owner-specified in both approaches
sections.applicability: Geotechnical analysis and corrosivity testing requirements for soil nail wall contract documents.

sections.title: Experience Requirements for Contractors
sections.summary: Selecting an experienced and qualified soil nail Contractor significantly increases the probability of a satisfactory installation. Key experience criteria include: completion of at least 5 similar soil nail wall projects; employment of a superintendent with at least 3 years of soil nail experience; use of drilling equipment and grouting methods appropriate for the soil conditions; and maintenance of a quality control program. Comprehensive construction specifications should address experience requirements, acceptable methods, and equipment.
sections.body: The practices used by the Contractor for soil nail wall construction need to provide a high-quality product and avoid conditions that could jeopardize wall integrity or create hazards. The likelihood of a satisfactory installation increases when an experienced and qualified soil nail Contractor with experienced personnel and good quality control procedures is selected, regardless of the construction method. The prospect of success further increases when comprehensive construction quality control (QC) and quality assurance (QA) programs are established. Typical experience requirements in specifications may include: completion of at least 5 comparable soil nail wall projects in the past 5 years; employment of a superintendent with at least 3 years of direct soil nail wall experience; use of drilling equipment appropriate for the site soils; and a documented QC program including daily installation logs, nail load testing program, and shotcrete testing.
key_points: Contractor experience is a key factor in soil nail wall construction success
Typical requirement: at least 5 comparable projects completed in past 5 years
Superintendent: minimum 3 years direct soil nail experience required
QC program: daily installation logs, nail load testing, shotcrete testing
Equipment: drilling and grouting equipment appropriate for site soil conditions
Comprehensive QC/QA specifications reduce risk regardless of contracting approach
sections.applicability: Contractor qualification and experience requirements for soil nail wall specifications.

sections.title: Procedural Specifications
sections.summary: In the Procedural (Method) approach, the Owner's design engineer prepares complete design drawings and specifications specifying all materials, dimensions, construction methods, and quality control requirements. This approach allows clear pricing comparisons between bidders and empowers the Owner's engineers to evaluate design options. It requires Owner engineering staff trained in soil nail wall design and construction, and the same staff becomes a valuable construction-phase resource when questions or design changes arise.
sections.body: The procedural contracting approach includes the development of a detailed set of plans and specifications to be provided in the bidding documents. Complete design details and specifications are developed so that each contractor submitting a bid has a defined product to price, making it straightforward for the Owner to compare pricing. This approach empowers the Owner's engineers to examine design options during design, but requires engineering staff trained in soil nail wall design and construction methods. The Owner's design staff becomes a valuable asset during construction when questions and/or design changes arise. Procedural specifications typically include: wall geometry and alignment; nail layout, length, inclination, and spacing; nail bar size and grade; grout mix design and injection pressure; corrosion protection class and details; shotcrete mix design and thickness; drainage details; and load testing requirements.
key_points: Owner's engineer provides complete design; Contractor prices a fully defined product
Advantage: straightforward bid comparison; Owner controls all design decisions
Requires Owner engineering staff experienced in soil nail design and construction
Specifications cover: nail geometry, grout, corrosion protection, shotcrete, drainage, testing
Owner's design staff is a valuable resource during construction for questions and changes
sections.applicability: Procedural (method) contracting approach for Owner-designed soil nail walls.

sections.title: Performance-Based Specifications
sections.summary: In the Performance-Based (Design/Build) approach, the Owner prepares geometric and aesthetic drawings, defines performance requirements (LRFD resistance factors, corrosion protection levels, deformation limits), and specifies acceptable design and construction methods. The Contractor performs the structural design and submits plans for Owner review. Bid quantities are based on line-and-grade drawings. This approach suits Owners without in-house soil nail design expertise and promotes contractor innovation, but requires sound performance specifications and robust review of Contractor submittals.
sections.body: The performance-based approach is often called line and grade, conceptual plans, or Design/Build. The Owner: (i) prepares drawings defining geometric and aesthetic requirements and material specifications for components; (ii) defines performance requirements including LRFD resistance factors, corrosion protection levels, and deformation limits; and (iii) indicates the range of acceptable design and construction methods. The Contractor performs the structural design and submits drawings and calculations for Owner review and approval before construction begins. Bid quantities are obtained from specified pay limits denoted on the line-and-grade drawings and can be bid on a lump-sum or unit-price basis per square foot of wall face. Special provisions may address: minimum experience requirements, acceptable computer programs and design methods, review periods for submittals, geotechnical baseline reports, load testing requirements, and construction monitoring requirements. A geotechnical baseline report may be provided to describe the subsurface conditions and reduce bid risk to the Contractor.
key_points: Owner defines geometry, performance criteria, and acceptable methods; Contractor designs
Performance criteria: LRFD resistance factors, corrosion protection class, deformation limits
Contractor submits design drawings and calculations for Owner review before construction
Bid quantities from line-and-grade drawings; can be lump sum or unit price per sq ft of face
Geotechnical baseline report may be provided to reduce Contractor subsurface risk
Requires sound specifications and rigorous review of Contractor design submittals
sections.applicability: Performance-based (Design/Build) contracting approach for soil nail walls where Contractor performs structural design.
